extractedItems.title: Penalty differences in stroke play and match play
extractedItems.question: If you break a rule during a stroke play competition, what is the general penalty?

choices.text: You go back to the tee
2 penalty strokes
Loss of hole
Extra shot with no penalty

extractedItems.explanation: In stroke play, the general penalty for a rule breach is 2 penalty strokes.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage girl in a sunny fairway setting holding a scorecard and looking thoughtful after realising she has broken a rule.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Teenage girl golfer on the fairway, reflecting after a rules breach.

extractedItems.title: What must you do with your ball on each hole?
extractedItems.question: In general, what must a player do with the ball they teed off with on each hole?

choices.text: Pick it up after a few shots
Change the ball on the green
Hole it out (play it into the hole)
Give up and move to the next hole

extractedItems.explanation: The ball that is teed off with must be played into the hole, otherwise the player could be disqualified.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage boy on the putting green lining up a short putt, making sure to finish holing out his original ball.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Teenage boy putting on the green with focus on holing out.

extractedItems.title: When can you change your golf ball?
extractedItems.question: Which situations allow you to substitute your golf ball while playing a hole?

choices.text: After you lose your ball
When taking relief
If your ball has a tiny scratch
If your ball is badly damaged (significant cut or crack)
At any moment, just because you want to

extractedItems.explanation: You can substitute your ball if it is lost, when taking relief, or if it's severely damaged. A small scratch doesn't count.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage girl on the fairway holding a severely cracked ball and preparing to replace it with a new one.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Teenage girl examining a cracked golf ball on the fairway.

choices.text: You have to return to the tee and replay the shot
You get 2 penalty strokes added to your score
You lose the hole
You retake the shot with no penalty

reviewedItems.explanation: In stroke play, the general penalty for a rule breach is 2 penalty strokes.

reviewedItems.title: What must you do with your ball on each hole?
reviewedItems.question: In general, what must a player do with the same ball they played from the tee on each hole?

choices.text: Pick it up after a few shots
Change it for a different one on the putting green
Play it into the hole (hole out)
Skip the putt if it's very short

reviewedItems.explanation: Players must play the same ball from the tee all the way into the hole, unless the rules allow them to change it.
reviewedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage boy lining up a putt on the green, focusing on playing his original ball into the hole for completion of the hole.
reviewedItems.imageAlt: Teenage boy putting on the green, concentrating on holing out.

reviewedItems.title: When can you change your golf ball?
reviewedItems.question: On which occasions are you allowed to replace your ball with another one while playing a hole?

choices.text: If you can't find your original ball after searching
When taking relief under the Rules (such as from a penalty area or abnormal course condition)
If your ball only has a small scratch
If your ball has a significant cut or crack
Any time you feel like it, even during play of a hole

reviewedItems.explanation: You may substitute a new ball if your original is lost, when taking relief under the rules, or if it's severely damaged (like a big cut or crack). A minor scratch isn't enough, and you can't just switch at any moment.
reviewedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage boy golfer standing on the fairway, examining a badly cracked golf ball before replacing it with a new one.
reviewedItems.imageAlt: Teenage boy inspecting a damaged golf ball on the fairway.
